targets.title: Investor reaction to covert corporate political activity
targets.evidence_quote: Exploiting a whistleblower's leak of the American Legislative Exchange Council's (ALEC) corporate sponsors, we quasi‐replicate and extend Werner's (2017) event study of investor reaction to covert corporate political activity (CPA).
targets.outcome_quote: Werner found that investors reacted positively to the accidental disclosure of covert ties to the Republican Governors Association. In contrast, when we apply the same research design to the ALEC leak, we find that, on average, firms tied to ALEC experienced negative abnormal returns.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract explicitly contrasts the central positive investor response in Werner with a negative response in the new event sample. Additional moderator findings are described as extensions, not as confirmations of this central effect.
